name: Dgraph
tagline: Distributed, horizontally scalable graph database in Go with native GraphQL and DQL.
description: Dgraph is an open-source distributed graph database written in Go that shards data by predicate across Raft groups and serves both a native GraphQL API (generated from your schema) and its own DQL query language. It provides distributed ACID transactions, full-text, geo and HNSW vector indexes, all now under Apache 2.0 after former enterprise features were opened up. Ownership changed twice: Hypermode acquired Dgraph Labs in 2024 and sold Dgraph to Istari Digital in October 2025, which committed to keep the open-source project going; v25 releases continue. It suits app backends that want GraphQL-native data with graph traversal, less so heavy analytics.

pricing.notes: Free and open source; commercial support available from the owner.

scale.notes: Predicates are sharded across Alpha groups with Raft replication; Zero nodes rebalance tablets automatically.

strengths: Native GraphQL: define a schema and get a working CRUD API without a resolver layer
Distributed ACID transactions with linearizable reads across shards
Predicate-based sharding with automatic tablet rebalancing
Fully Apache 2.0, including ACLs, encryption at rest and CDC
Built-in full-text, geo, regex and HNSW vector indexes
weaknesses: Two ownership changes since 2024 add uncertainty about long-term direction
DQL is unique to Dgraph, so skills and queries do not transfer
Predicate sharding makes very high-degree predicates hot spots
Weaker for whole-graph analytics compared with dedicated analytics engines
